title: Xbox XP biriminin başına Kayleen Walters getirildi, Mojang'ın yeni CEO'su açıklandı
summary: Xbox'ın oyun ötesi eğlence birimi XP'nin başkanlığına Kayleen Walters getirilirken, Mojang'ın yeni CEO'su Maria Angelidou-Smith oldu.
body:
Xbox, oyun dünyasının ötesine geçerek film, dizi, canlı etkinlikler ve ürün ortaklıklarına odaklanacak **Xbox XP** biriminin yönetim kadrosunu netleştirdi. Wccftech ve IGN'in aktardığına göre, oyun markalarını sinema ve eğlence sektöründe büyütmeyi amaçlayan bu yeni birimin başına Lucasfilm ve Mojang deneyimli Kayleen Walters getirildi.

## XP birimi ve yeni atamalar

Deneyimli isim Kayleen Walters liderliğindeki XP birimi; Xbox Pictures, Xbox Products, Xbox Partnerships ve Xbox Places olmak üzere dört ana alana odaklanacak. Bu yapılanma kapsamında Minecraft'ın geliştiricisi Mojang'da da bayrak değişimi yaşandı. Walters'tan boşalan Mojang CEO'su koltuğuna, Meta, Personio ve Reddit'teki geçmiş görevleriyle tanınan **Maria Angelidou-Smith** atandı.

## Gelecek projeler ve strateji

Microsoft'un dünyadaki en büyük eğlence şirketi olma hedefi doğrultusunda kurulan XP birimi; Minecraft Squared devam filmi, Fallout üçüncü sezonu, Call of Duty filmi, Netflix'in Diablo animasyon serisi ve Hideo Kojima imzalı Physint projesi gibi yapımları doğru ortaklarla buluşturacak. Walters'ın yeni ekibine gönderdiği epostada hayranların bu serileri sadece oynamadığını, aynı zamanda izleyip giydiğini ve kutladığını vurguladığı belirtildi.

**Neden önemli?** Microsoft, popüler oyun serilerinin sinema ve televizyon uyarlamalarındaki başarılarını yapım ortaklıklarıyla sürekli kılmayı hedeflerken, Mojang yönetimine teknoloji ve topluluk odaklı yeni bir lider kazandırıyor.

source_texts.text:
Xbox wants to turn its biggest franchises into far more than games. We've known that for a while, but in a new company-wide email (available in its entirety on Xbox Wire), the explosive new CEO Asha Sharma has just announced XP, a new division focused on how people experience Xbox franchises beyond the games themselves.
The name is a play on Experience Points, of course. The division will focus on four main areas of investment:
- Xbox Pictures, covering film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling
- Xbox Products, covering licensing and merchandise
- Xbox Partnerships, covering sponsors, brands, and creator collaborations
- Xbox Places, covering broadcasts, live events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences
Leading XP as President is Kayleen Walters, who moves over from Mojang. Her resume makes the appointment an obvious fit: before joining Xbox, she spent 13 years at Lucasfilm helping guide Star Wars across films, products, and partnerships. At Minecraft, she grew consumer products into a multibillion-dollar business with more than 250 licensees, and served as executive producer of A Minecraft Movie, which Sharma notes was the biggest film in the US last year and a top-five release worldwide. She's also a producer on the upcoming sequel.
The Ambition: Xbox as the Number One in Entertainment
Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball laid out the bigger picture in a separate blog post, stating that Xbox's ambition is simply to become the number one entertainment company in the world. XP, he explained, brings together capabilities that have existed across various Xbox teams for years, aligning them around a shared mission to help its franchises reach more people.
Notably, XP isn't a production company. According to The Hollywood Reporter, its role is to match Xbox's IP with the right production partners, with the aim of replicating the success of adaptations like Fallout and A Minecraft Movie for Xbox's biggest franchises, including Call of Duty, Warcraft, Gears of War, Candy Crush, Diablo, Forza, The Elder Scrolls, and Halo. In an email to her new team, Walters said fans don't just play these franchises: "They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them."
There's already plenty in the pipeline. Minecraft has a movie sequel (titled Minecraft Squared) in production, as well as a theme park planned for 2027. A Call of Duty movie from Taylor Sheridan and Peter Berg is in the works, Netflix has announced a Diablo animated series at BlizzCon 2026, and Fallout's third season is on the way at Amazon. Even PHYSINT, the Hideo Kojima game Xbox picked up after Sony walked away, is already looking toward film and TV adaptations, just like their other joint project, the horror-themed OD.
Not everything has worked, of course. Paramount's Halo series was a failure (even though the second season was an improvement over the first one), which arguably makes the case for a dedicated division to manage these adaptations more carefully.
A New CEO for Mojang
Walters' move also left a vacancy at Mojang, which Sharma has already filled with Maria Angelidou-Smith as the new CEO of Mojang and Minecraft. She spent nearly a decade at Meta, where she led Facebook Groups, used by more than 1.8 billion people each month, along with Events, Creators, Search, Profile, and Monetization. She later led product and technology at Personio and served as Chief Product Officer at Reddit.
Sharma explained that Mojang already has an exceptional development team, so the search focused on someone deeply technical with experience building products for communities at an enormous scale. Angelidou-Smith's first priority will be learning from the teams and communities who know Minecraft best. Both Walters and Angelidou-Smith will report directly to Sharma, in the latest sweeping decision made by the Xbox CEO since she joined the division in February.

source_texts.title: Xbox Announces New XP Entertainment Division to Make Movies, TV, and More
source_texts.summary: Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post at Minecraft maker Mojang, for whom she was president – and also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.
source_texts.text:
Xbox has announced a new TV, movies, and entertainment division called XP. It will be headed up by Kayleen Walters, a Lucasfilm veteran who moves over from her most recent post as president of Minecraft maker Mojang, where she also served as an executive producer on last year's A Minecraft Movie.
XP brings together four "areas of investment": Xbox Pictures; Xbox Products; Xbox Partnerships; and Xbox Places. Microsoft said XP was set up to help Xbox become the number one entertainment and gaming company in the world, which requires broadening its big franchises beyond video games themselves. But it is not a production company. Rather, Microsoft wants to find the right partners to work across film, TV, physical experiences, and consumer products.
Microsoft has already seen significant success in the movie and TV space, with Warner Bros.' A Minecraft Movie breaking box office records, and Amazon's Fallout TV show setting records for Prime Video. Upcoming Xbox adaptations include movie sequel Minecraft Squared, Fallout Season 3, a Call of Duty movie with Peter Berg and Taylor Sheridan, and a Diablo animated series with Netflix. Microsoft's deal for Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint includes film and TV rights, so expect an adaptation of that eventually.
XP is also about live events, and again, Xbox already has success there. Blizzard's BlizzCon saw a number of significant announcements, with 35,000 people at the physical event in Anaheim, California, and 12.5 million watching at home. The most recent Minecraft Live, which saw the announcement of the first new dimension for Minecraft in 14 years, reached more than 144 million people.
Meanwhile, Microsoft cited partnerships such as Gears of War's takeover with WWE, and Xbox's range of Ikea furniture. A Minecraft theme park is set to open its gates next year.
"XP was created from a simple but powerful belief: the world's most beloved gaming franchises have an opportunity to reach people far beyond the boundaries of the game itself," Walters said. "Fans don't just play our franchises. They watch them, wear them, attend them, celebrate them, and connect with them in countless ways. XP brings together the teams responsible for helping Xbox franchises show up in the world in bigger, more meaningful ways."
"XP is a play on 'Experience Points' and formalizes four investment areas for us: Xbox Pictures for film and television adaptations; Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise; Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners; and Xbox Places for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote in a company-wide memo also posted to Xbox Wire.
"Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place."
Microsoft noted the uplift its video games can get when movies and shows do well. For example, Fallout games on Game Pass saw a 5x increase in hours played during Fallout Season 1. Minecraft, meanwhile, saw over a 75% increase in weekly active users year-over-year since the movie released (as of April 30, 2026).
If this sounds a bit familiar, it's because Microsoft has tried this before. In 2012 (back in the Xbox 360 era!), Microsoft announced Xbox Entertainment Studios with an aim to produce TV shows that would air directly on Xbox consoles. XES revealed plans to create shows based on Gears of War, Fable, Forza, and State of Decay — not to mention, of course, the original version of the Halo TV show announced at E3 by Stephen Spielberg, who was set to executive produce. They even planned to make an unscripted street-soccer drama called Every Street United. The entire XES effort lasted just two years before getting shut down as the Xbox One's "all in one" message failed to resonate with gamers following its reveal in 2013.
As part of the changes, Mojang has a new boss. Maria Angelidou-Smith, who joins Xbox as CEO of Mojang, spent nearly a decade at Meta working on Facebook Groups before stints at Personio and Reddit, where she was Chief Product Officer. "She has built products used by billions of people and led product and engineering organizations through significant growth and change," Sharma said.
"She will bring that experience to Mojang while learning from the people who know Minecraft best. Her first order of business is for her to learn from the teams and communities that make Minecraft so special."
Minecraft is, of course, one of the big Xbox franchises the company is doubling down on amid Sharma's ongoing "Reset," which has seen nearly 2,000 staff cut from the gaming business so far this financial year. Minecraft is the best-selling video game of all time, having shifted over 425 million copies. Its significant merchandising business became one of the top 20 globally.
